en.title: Largest House Area
en.description:
In the grid, 1 represents a roof and 0 represents open ground. Only 1s adjacent up, down, left or right belong to the same house; diagonal cells are not connected. Find the number of cells covered by the largest house.

The original problem's connectivity rule is clear; this site adds the grid size and the result for a grid with no houses.

Source: https://oamaster.com/docs/companies/hsbc#3-find-largest-house-area (pinned statement fingerprint bc491c62512372ce7be7577a7bddababee74bfcb3e6c5f6a6e16ba8ae3e85292). The input/output protocol and bounds added by this site are as described in the statement and are not claimed to be the original site's rules.
en.input: The first line contains n m (1≤n,m, and nm≤200000); each of the next n lines contains m values, each 0 or 1.
en.output: Output the area of the largest connected component; output 0 if there is no 1.
en.explanation: See the accompanying notes for the full approach, proof and complexity.
hints: For each unvisited 1, run a four-direction BFS/DFS, count the size of its component and update the maximum.
